Full summary: Implemented #16: twining-semantic-review plugin skill (LLM-judged staleness, skill-driven option a) plus twining_archive_stale per-item reasons map for the audit trail. Plugin bumped 1.13.0 → 1.14.0. 1198 tests green.
Decisions: Chose the skill-driven path for #16 (option a from the issue: the session's own model judges staleness inside a user-invoked skill) over wiring an Anthropic SDK client into the server (option b) — keeps the MCP server free of model dependencies and API-key config, gives the user transparent control over what the model sees, and the issue author already leaned this way.; Chose to satisfy the per-item audit-trail criterion by adding an optional reasons map (id → rationale) to twining_archive_stale rather than packing per-item text into the existing single reason string — structured input survives formatting changes and only reasons for actually-archived ids are recorded.; Chose auto-invocable: false and an explicit never-as-a-side-effect rule in the skill — #16's acceptance criteria require no model judgment without explicit opt-in, and archival is the one Twining operation that destroys context for future agents.; Chose to have the skill degrade gracefully in lite tool surface (decisions via twining_why + dangling warnings via housekeeping) since twining_read is full-surface only — mirrors the twining-verify skill's existing pattern for surface-gated tools.
Findings: Acceptance criteria 1-2 of #16 (dead concept flagged, active concept not flagged) are model-judgment behaviors encoded as verification rules in the skill prompt (grep-verify before scoring >0.8, never flag concepts present in the repo) — they need field validation on a real aged project, not unit tests.; Skills are auto-discovered from plugin/skills/ — no plugin.json registration needed; BEHAVIORS.md does not document skills.
